title: Rabbi Zekharyah, Son-in-Law of Rabbi Levi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (A Palestinian Amora of the third generation.) In halakhah he is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim, beginning of chapter 1, where he said: “It was taught: A menstruant washes her hair,” etc. There, 2:2: “Rabbi Yehudah ben Pazi asked … Rabbi Zekharyah, son-in-law of Rabbi Levi, said: It is a dispute of Rabbi Meir and the sages”; and so it is in Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:4. In Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:1, folio 4b: “Rabbi Zekharyah, son-in-law of Rabbi Levi, asked … Rabbi Chananya son of Rabbi Hillel ben Pazi said: Was it not already refuted there? And Rabbi Yose (Rabbi Yonah’s colleague) said: It stands,” etc. In Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:1: “Rabbi Zavdi (Hyman proposes Rabbi Zekharyah), son-in-law of Rabbi Levi, asked … Rabbi Yose said: Explain it,” etc.

In aggadah he is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5, where he said to those youths who were dismissed from school and went out to the villages … In Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1, he said: “Like a person who calls a blind man ‘one of abundant light.’” In Midrash Shmuel 2:3 Hyman considers Rabbi Zavdiya an erroneous reading. In Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 1:4: “Rabbi Zavdiya (Hyman proposes Rabbi Zekharyah), son-in-law of Rabbi Levi, related this incident,” etc. In the Jerusalem Talmud, end of Peah, and Shekalim 5:6, it is related that they slandered him, saying that he did not need to take from charity yet took; and when he died it was found that everything he took he gave to others.

notes.text: סיפרא is school, and the speech is addressed to the youths, not about children withdrawing from a scroll. Saved Guggenheimer Taanit4:5 contains the connected paragraph. ר״ל is Levi by the full heading, not Resh Lakish; Zavdi/Zavdiya alternatives remain Hyman’s proposed corrections.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5 paragraph directly addresses youths leaving school for the villages. Hyman’s Zavdi/Zavdiya-to-Zekharyah corrections, the third-generation placement and the combined charity notice remain attributed rather than automatic name harmonizations.
